newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call surges on new special advance pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call surges on new special advance pact.

text.p: Dutch call money surged almost 40 basis points on Friday, following the allocation of a new seven-day special advances pact and an outflow of payments for Dutch treasury certificates (DTCs).
The Dutch central bank had allocated 4.39 billion guilders on a seven-day pact. Other money market rates were unchanged.
While the previous special advances pact was seen as generous, dealers were divided about the relative size of the new pact and its influence on the rise in call money.
"The allocation was less ample than the previous one," said one dealer.
"The allocation has to be seen in the light of DTC payments that have to be made today," said another.
Market participants said that since the state had been quite active in issuing DTCs recently, part of the rise in call money probably reflected payments to the state.
"The rise in call (money) goes far beyond the usual end-of-the-week effect," said a trader. "That effect accounts for no more than some 0.08 of the total rise," he added.
Volume picked up again, especially in the short end up to one month. Dealers cited retail activity.
Dealers said they were unsure about how money rates were likely to move next week, with some saying that call could remain high on DTC payments.
Overnight guilders were up at 2.75 percent bid, from 2.38 percent on Thursday.
Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.92 percent bid.
The guilder firmed a little to 112.13 per 100 marks.
